card.line: Gilgal was Israel's first camp after crossing the Jordan into Canaan, and it later became a place where Saul was made king and then failed.

moments.title: Twelve stones at Gilgal
moments.text: After crossing the Jordan on dry ground, Israel camped at Gilgal. Joshua set up the twelve stones taken from the river to remind children of what the LORD did.

moments.title: The reproach of Egypt rolled away
moments.text: At Gilgal Joshua circumcised the sons of Israel, who had been born in the wilderness. The LORD said He had rolled away the reproach of Egypt, and the place was called Gilgal.

moments.title: Passover in the land
moments.text: Camped at Gilgal on the plains of Jericho, the Israelites kept the Passover. The next day they ate the land's produce, and the manna stopped.

moments.title: Saul confirmed as king
moments.text: Samuel called the people to Gilgal to renew the kingship. There they confirmed Saul as king before the LORD, offered peace offerings, and rejoiced greatly.

moments.title: Saul's offering and loss of kingdom
moments.text: Saul waited seven days for Samuel at Gilgal, but his troops began to desert. He offered the burnt offering himself, and Samuel said his kingdom would not endure because he did not keep the LORD's command.
